courses.title: Introduction to Public Speaking
courses.description: Part 1: In this course, students learn and apply foundational rhetorical theories and techniques of public speaking in a multicultural democratic society. Students discover, develop, and critically analyze ideas in public discourse through research, reasoning, organization, composition, delivery to a live audience and evaluation of various types of speeches, including informative and persuasive speeches.

courses.title: Intercultural Communication - HONORS
courses.description: Intercultural Communication is an introduction to interaction across cultural divides in domestic and global contexts. This course examines how differing cultures, languages, and social patterns influence the way members of groups relate among themselves and with members of other ethnic and cultural groups. Intercultural Communication emphasizes the development of interpersonal skills for communicating effectively across cultures and encourages appreciation of diverse cultural voices. As an honors course, students will be expected to complete additional assignments to gain deeper insight into the critical praxis of Intercultural Communication.

courses.title: Argumentation and Critical Inquiry in Oral Communication - HONORS
courses.description: This course presents the principles and methods of critical inquiry, advocacy, and debate. Students will develop research skills; critically evaluate evidence; identify fallacies in reasoning and language; advance reasoned positions with consideration to ethical practices and cultural sensitivity; and use critical thinking to defend and refute arguments through analysis, presentation, and evaluation of oral and written communication arguments. This is an honors course.

courses.description: This course covers critical reading, writing, and thinking. Research strategies, documentation, critical analysis, and synthesis in the process of evaluating and constructing oral and written arguments will be applied. courses.title: Critical Decision-Making in Groups - HONORS
courses.description: This course is the study of communication and critical thinking in the context of effective group problem-solving with an emphasis on principles of information literacy and sound reasoning to make a well-reasoned decision. This course explores the theory, application, and evaluation of group communication processes, including problem-solving, conflict management, decision-making, and leadership, with the goal of understanding different points of view in an increasingly diverse and interconnected global society. This is an honors course.

courses.title: Interpersonal Communication - HONORS
courses.description: This course focuses on the study of interpersonal communication theory, methods, and research, with an emphasis on developing self-concept through listening, verbal and nonverbal communication, language, and cultural knowledge to ethically maintain effective relationships in an increasingly diverse and interconnected global society, both personally and professionally. This is an honors course.

courses.title: Argumentation and Critical Inquiry in Oral Communication
courses.description: This course presents the principles and methods of critical inquiry, advocacy, and debate. Students will develop research skills, critically evaluate evidence, identify fallacies in reasoning and language, advance reasoned positions with consideration to ethical practices and cultural sensitivity, and use critical thinking to defend and refute arguments through analysis, presentation, and evaluation of oral and written communication arguments.

courses.title: Critical Decision-Making in Groups
courses.description: This course is the study of communication and critical thinking in the context of effective group problem-solving with an emphasis on principles of information literacy and sound reasoning to make a well-reasoned decision. This course explores the theory, application, and evaluation of group communication processes, including problem-solving, conflict management, decision-making, and leadership, with the goal of understanding different points of view in an increasingly diverse and interconnected global society.

courses.title: Performance Studies
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the theories and methods of performance studies with a focus on oral interpretation. There is an emphasis placed on understanding how oral interpretation performances reflect and reconstitute the values and beliefs of diverse cultures. Students will analyze how members of various ethnic or cultural groups contribute to knowledge, civilization, and society through oral interpretation.
courses.advisories: ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.

metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Identify how oral interpretation performances have shaped and continue to constitute the values, beliefs, and practices of diverse cultures. Critically analyze the philosophical, historical, literary, aesthetic, and cultural importance of oral interpretation performances through shared feedback and self-reflections. Critically examine and implement performance theory within oral interpretation performances and oral interpretation scripts.
